paragraph: A carrier entering India normally has three commercial decisions to make: which routes to sell, which agency or cargo channels to activate, and which responsibilities to delegate locally. For passenger operations, compare sales potential by city pair and cabin. For cargo, use lane demand and uplift capacity to set forwarder priorities. Agree the reporting and approval structure before the trade launch.
checklist: Choose the initial routes and traffic segments|List the channel partners able to sell and service the product|Assign an airline-side owner for rates, approvals and escalations

section: What to put in an airline GSA mandate
paragraph: A commercial mandate should make the representative’s limits clear. For example, a GSA might lead agency training and account development while the carrier retains fare approval, settlement oversight and disruption decisions. Ask bidders to explain account ownership, how changes are approved, and what records the airline receives when the engagement ends.
checklist: Document territory, term and exclusivity|Define what the representative can approve|Agree a monthly pipeline and sales report

section: What to prepare for an India trade launch
paragraph: A foreign carrier can begin commercial discovery before publishing a route, using a shortlist of agencies and corporate buyers to test product fit. Mark schedule, fare and servicing assumptions clearly in internal materials. Release a trade offer only after the airline has confirmed inventory, sale dates and the approved point of contact.
checklist: Test agency demand by city pair|Agree who handles buyer questions and escalations|Check that trade materials reflect confirmed inventory and sale dates

section: How to choose passenger distribution channels
paragraph: Compare travel agencies, consolidators and corporate travel managers by their ability to sell your routes and service bookings. A consolidator may deliver reach across independent agencies, while direct corporate accounts can require negotiated eligibility, reporting and a named support owner. Set a practical booking baseline before judging the channel’s performance.
checklist: Review sales potential by route and cabin|Confirm ticketing and servicing responsibilities|Track both activated accounts and flown revenue

section: What to include in a cargo lane brief
paragraph: Start with origin and destination, indicative uplift, commodity mix, cut-off times and allocation rules. Share the brief with forwarders that can provide shipment forecasts and can work within the carrier’s acceptance process. Review handling, claims and exception ownership with the carrier before any rate or space commitment goes to market.
checklist: Set allocation limits by route|Record commodity acceptance and handling constraints|Compare quoted shipments with flown tonnage

paragraph: Separate demand testing, distribution setup and launch approval into stages. Use the first stage to identify viable buyer segments and the second to confirm that agents can display and service the product. Keep dates for marketing and trade announcements tied to airline-confirmed inventory and the carrier’s approved readiness process.
checklist: Validate demand with trade accounts|Test booking and servicing flows with pilot partners|Approve the trade launch date with the carrier

section: How to structure the feasibility comparison
paragraph: Build scenarios for cautious, expected and stronger demand. Distinguish local origin-and-destination traffic from connecting passengers, then stress-test how seasonality, flight timings and a competitor schedule change could affect each scenario. Keep a record of the source and date for each assumption so the commercial team can update the model.
checklist: Compare alternative departure times|Separate local traffic and onward feed|Record the demand, average fare and capacity assumptions

section: Where to start Delhi NCR account development
paragraph: Build separate lists for Delhi-area corporate buyers, travel management companies and consolidators. Assess each account against the planned routes and its ability to handle service changes. Use a first-quarter plan to distinguish training activity from actual quotes, bookings and corporate agreements.
checklist: Identify target accounts by itinerary and cabin need|Check how buyers handle booking changes|Review quotes and flown activity by account

section: How to qualify Mumbai airline accounts
paragraph: Map travellers and freight buyers around the carrier’s BOM network. Separate corporate accounts, leisure consolidators and freight forwarders so each group sees relevant schedules, terms and support contacts. Give ownership of follow-up to one person per account and record where there is an existing airline relationship.
checklist: Segment passenger and cargo prospects|Confirm route fit and decision-maker ownership|Track opportunities through quotation and confirmed activity
